summary:
Imo is a state in south-eastern Nigeria and stands under the national legal framework. Its own record covers enforcement action taken inside the state against private gatherings and against people accused of same-sex conduct in public.

On 26 April 2018 two men in Imo State were stripped, beaten and paraded through the streets after being accused of gay sex. An inquiry by NoStringsNG found that the victims were then arrested by the police themselves, and that they might need legal support. The state's role in the episode was to detain the people who had been attacked, not the crowd that attacked them.

Enforcement continued into 2025. On 19 February the Imo Police Command broke up a party at Graziella Hotels in Orogwe, Owerri West, arrested many of those present, described as gay and lesbian suspects, and placed attendees who fled on a police search list. The event was a private hotel gathering, and the police treated it as an operation with names attached to people who were not detained.

Seven years separate the two documented episodes, and they occurred in different parts of the state: a street in 2018, a hotel in Owerri West in 2025. Police action in Imo is therefore not confined to a single locality, and it has not been limited to public conduct. Both a public street and a closed private venue appear in the record as points of exposure, and leaving before an arrest did not remove people from the search.
tangentialFactors:
No source in the inventory counts enforcement operations in Imo. The two documented episodes are those that reached publication, and the inventory does not establish how frequently the Imo Police Command acts against gatherings.

Both men and women fell within the description of those arrested in February 2025, and the search list extended the operation beyond the people detained. A person who was not at the venue can remain part of the police investigation.

An accusation of same-sex conduct in Imo carries a legal consequence independent of any crowd violence that accompanies it: the two men beaten and paraded in 2018 were arrested by the police, and an inquiry concluded that they might need legal support.
localsOnly:
Residents accused of same-sex conduct in Imo have faced mob punishment followed by police detention rather than police protection. The April 2018 inquiry concluded that the two victims might need legal support.

The February 2025 operation gives residents a second exposure: a private gathering was treated as police intelligence, those present were arrested, and those who left were added to a search list. Absence from the venue at the time of the operation does not remove a resident from the investigation.

The operation was directed at a hotel event in Owerri West, which places organisers, hosts and venue staff within the same enforcement target as attendees.
outOfScopeNotes:
No source in the inventory records charges, trial outcomes or sentences for the two men arrested in Imo in April 2018, nor for those detained at Orogwe in February 2025. Whether prosecutions followed, and under which provision, is unresolved.

Which statutory provision the Imo Police Command applied in the 2025 operation is not stated in the inventory.

The inventory holds no Imo-specific reporting on healthcare access, document or marker rules, custodial placement, or protection for transgender residents, and no Imo-specific instance of app-based entrapment or of violence against a transgender person in the state.

Whether any court in Imo applies religious or customary penalties for same-sex conduct is not addressed by any source here.
